mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the next 20 trading days signals an easing monetary policy cycle, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d forward returns are not significantly higher than a 60-day rolling average during the easing period (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS rises in the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 3.5% in the next month signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing growth expectations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d forward returns are positive despite UNRATE crossing above 3.5%, or the rate rise does not persist beyond 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% triggers a tightening cycle, raising interest rates and dampening equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5d forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS exceeding 4.5%, or the rate increase reverses within 5 days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST (demand) and INDPRO (supply) over the next 5 days signals robust economic activity, boosting equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and INDPRO both increasing from their latest available values
failure_condition: S&P 500 5d forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite both proxies increasing, or one proxy increases while the other decreases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in INDPRO (supply) and decrease in UNRATE (labor) over the next month signals strong production growth and labor market stability, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous available value and UNRATE < previous available value
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite the supply-labor combination, or the proxies move in opposite directions.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decline in FEDFUNDS below 1.5% triggers stronger easing, amplifying equity valuations and resulting in significantly higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, S&P 500 60d forward returns are not significantly higher than a 60-day rolling average (t-test p > 0.05) despite FEDFUNDS falling below 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PAYEMS above 152,383 in the next month signals a robust labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5d forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite PAYEMS exceeding 152,383, or the increase reverses within 5 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery regime, a decline in FEDFUNDS below 1.5% combined with UNRATE below 3.5% signals coordinated policy easing and labor market normalization, driving substantial positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5d forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) despite both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE falling below their thresholds in the post-shock regime, or the proxies move in opposite directions.
